skill.name: teardown
skill.description: Creates technical illustrations of physical objects and of how things work, such as display pixels or interface layers, with coherent views, fine linework and part fills.
skill.summary: Create evidence-based technical illustrations with assembled views, exploded views, interactive controls, and SVG, PNG, and PDF exports.
skill.author: jakubkrehel

content.value_statement: Complex objects and layered concepts are difficult to explain with disconnected images. Teardown builds coherent technical illustrations with interactive views and portable drawing exports.
actual_capabilities: Construct meshes with lathes, extrusions, lofts, sweeps, springs, and reusable part helpers.
Project one model into assembled and exploded drawings with hidden-line removal.
Provide spacing, parameter, annotation, linework, color, and part-isolation controls in a standalone HTML viewer.
Export selected drawing states as SVG, 300 dpi PNG, and vector PDF, with crop and transparency options.
Generate proof sheets across parameter extremes and warn about heavily occluded exploded parts.
Check generated pages in local Chrome for rendering errors, missing parts, and unexpected network requests.
limitations: Illustrations are not manufacturing drawings and do not establish tolerances, material specifications, or drafting compliance.
Photographs cannot establish hidden construction or exact dimensions; unsupported details must remain omitted or explicitly illustrative.
Viewer builds require Node and installed PDF and font dependencies; browser checks require Node 22 or later and Chrome.
Model scripts must be trusted, and imported SVG needs sanitization; PDF labels fall back to Helvetica.

use_cases.title: Explain Product Assemblies
use_cases.description: Create assembled and exploded views with stable part names, component isolation, and downloadable technical illustrations.

use_cases.title: Teach Layered Concepts
use_cases.description: Represent display pixels or interface layers as colored plates with adjustable spacing and annotations.
use_cases.target_user: Educators explaining physical or digital systems

use_cases.title: Present Product Concepts
use_cases.description: Build parameterized concept illustrations and inspect component placement before sharing a portable viewer.

prompt_templates.title: Illustrate a Simple Object
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a technical illustration of [object] from [reference]. Mark estimated proportions and provide a standalone viewer with SVG and PNG exports.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: illustrate one object from a supplied reference.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an Assembly
prompt_templates.prompt: Illustrate [assembly] from [sources]. Build assembled and exploded views from one model, name each part, and identify unsupported internal details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: explain how multiple components fit together.

prompt_templates.title: Visualize a Layered Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Represent [concept] as named colored layers. Include spacing and annotation controls, mark the drawing as conceptual, and verify SVG, PNG, and PDF exports.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn an abstract system into a layered illustration.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Verify Parameterized Views
prompt_templates.prompt: Build [assembly] using [authoritative references]. Expose [parameters] within [ranges], preserve mating features, proof all extremes, and report export defects and assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate a parameterized model and its deliverables.

output_examples.input: Illustrate a fictional hinge with assembled and exploded views.
output: A standalone viewer shows named hinge leaves, a pin, and an illustrative spring.
Spacing, annotations, component colors, and isolated-part SVG downloads are available.
The evidence record identifies invented dimensions and concept construction.

output_examples.input: Explain a simplified display pixel as colored layers.
output: A conceptual drawing separates the backlight, matrix, color filters, and cover glass.
A spacing control reveals the layers while assembled mode restores their arrangement.
SVG, PNG, and PDF downloads preserve the selected view and colors.

best_practices: Record supplied dimensions, estimated proportions, and illustrative construction separately before modeling.
Use trusted model scripts and sanitize imported SVG before embedding it in the viewer.
Inspect rendered sheets at delivery size and close range, then verify parameter extremes and downloaded files.
anti_patterns: Inventing hidden construction from a photograph and presenting it as verified product geometry.
Treating a fitted illustration as a toleranced manufacturing drawing or a verified numeric scale.
Claiming visual or export verification after only checking source code or successful file generation.

faq.question: What references can I provide?
faq.answer: Provide descriptions, photographs, CAD models, product drawings, or concepts. State which references establish geometry and which only establish visual style.

faq.question: Can the drawings be used for manufacturing?
faq.answer: No. The workflow produces illustrations, not toleranced manufacturing drawings. Use a CAD drawing workflow for fabrication requirements.

faq.question: Which files can the viewer export?
faq.answer: The viewer exports editable SVG, 300 dpi PNG, and vector PDF. It supports selected colors, tight crops, transparency, and isolated-part SVG downloads.

faq.question: Does the generated viewer need a server?
faq.answer: No. The bundled builder embeds scripts, libraries, and fonts so the page opens from disk without runtime network requests.

faq.question: What tools are needed to build and verify it?
faq.answer: Building needs Node and the documented font and PDF packages. Browser checks need Node 22 or later and local Chrome or Chromium.

faq.question: Can I run model scripts from an unknown source?
faq.answer: No. Model scripts are executable generator source, not safely sandboxed input. Review them first and sanitize external SVG before embedding.
